title: The Tel Ḥevron 2014 Excavations: Final Report (Ariel University Institute of Archaeology Monograph Series No. 1)
author: Emanuel Eisenberg; David Ben-Shlomo (eds.)
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted excavation final report. Project stores its own summary of the reported stratigraphic/fortification findings only; no reproduction of plans, section drawings, or photographs.
summary: Final report of Eisenberg's 1999 and 2014 salvage excavations at Tell Rumeida (with Ben-Shlomo), exposing further stretches of the Middle Bronze Age 'cyclopean' city wall (independently dated by pottery and scarabs from associated floors to MB II, c. 1750-1550 BCE) and later Iron II fortification elements — a glacis/rampart system, a parallel supporting wall, and a tower — that the editors compare typologically to Iron II fortifications at Tell el-Ful and Tell Beit Mirsim, both dated in the late 8th-7th centuries BCE (the Judahite state period, including a probable Hezekiah-era reinforcement phase). A Hebrew seal and an ostracon fragment recovered in these seasons are likewise Iron II but not closely dated to the 10th century specifically. This project's finding from this report: the site's well-excavated, clearly-dated fortification horizons cluster at Middle Bronze Age (the cyclopean wall itself) and at the later Iron II Judahite-state period (8th-7th centuries BCE); only scattered, non-diagnostic remains are attributed to the intervening Iron I / early Iron IIA (11th-10th century BCE) window that would correspond to 2 Samuel 2's setting — no excavated town plan, gate, or fortification specific to that narrower horizon is reported here.
confidenceNotes: Bibliographic details (editors, publisher, series, year) and the fortification-comparison findings are drawn from secondary web citations describing this report's contents (academic abstracts and citing papers referencing specific page ranges within it), not from direct inspection of the 474-page final report itself. TO VERIFY: direct confirmation of the Iron I/early Iron IIA scarcity claim against the report's own stratigraphic tables, and exact page citations for the fortification chapter. 2026-08-11 (queue #20d): re-checked specifically for Iron Age water installations relevant to claim-hebron-pool-feature (the 'pool of Hebron,' 2 Samuel 4:12). This report's 2014-season findings do include cisterns and water channels at the site (per secondary summaries), but none independently confirmed as Iron Age in the material found here — the report's published water-related feature is a Second Temple-period ritual bath/mikveh, and its Iron II fortification-period discussion (glacis/tower, 8th-7th century BCE) does not mention an associated water installation. No Iron Age pool or cistern is confirmed at the site in this pass. TO VERIFY against the report's own water-system chapter/plans directly.
